kept.spine: The arrangements at Spitzplatz are sufficient and nothing in them is spare. One more call on them and the town would be choosing which pressure to leave uncovered.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls with NO force
kept.spine: The walls are kept up and no soldier of the town's own stands behind them.
faces: {elders} {v:take} the walls for their own boundary before anything else, and where the line runs is the older argument.
A night patrolman says the walls are somebody's charge and the walk along the top of them is nobody's, and he goes up after dark regardless.
A clerk of the court says the walls come before it only as a question of who owes the work, and never as a question of who would hold them.
The people of the town have seen the walls kept up and nobody standing on them, and they take it that no one is expected.

kept.poolKey: Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)
kept.spine: A complaint brought here is heard in a court, and the man complained of can be held until it is.
faces: A man who sits on the council holds that a man waits at the court because the matter before his is being heard properly.
A drover says a man waits at the court because nobody has said whose business he is.
Asked at the court, a bailiff says a stranger's complaint is heard in the same order as anyone else's, and whether the stranger stays for it is the stranger's own affair.
A woman at the long table reckons a man is called in for who he knows and let out for what he can pay.
One of the watch says the wage is the same whether the night is quiet or a man has to be walked to the cell.
A soldier reckons a stranger stopped at the gate is the garrison's until his business is asked. After that he is the watch's.
The dyers' warden says the trades pay for the waiting twice, in the man held and in the work that stands still with him.
The stallholders say a stranger cheated in the square is told where to bring it, and a stallholder cheated by a stranger is told the same after the stranger is gone.
The men who hold the way in say a stranger with a complaint against him waits at the gate until somebody comes down from the court for him.

kept.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only
kept.spine: The grain store here stands against a bad harvest. No sick house stands with it, and what nursing is done is the parish's.
faces: A local priest says a stranger asks where the sick house is and is given a person instead, and nobody born here asks for the house at all.
Grain is hard to keep for anybody in the town without a door of their own to keep it behind, a woman who sells at the market says.
An innkeeper reckons strangers walk up to look at the grain store and nobody who lives here troubles to.
A man who walks the circuit says he is asked where the grain is kept by every stranger and where the sick are taken by none.
A master of one of the crafts says what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
One who waits on the court says a stranger's questions about the grain store are ordinary and the ones about the sick are new to him.

kept.spine: Some parts of the town are safe and some are not, and the people here know which are which. A thinner watch, or a bolder hand on the other side of it, would move that line and nothing else would need to change.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: What the town says of its own safety is what it says to anyone newly come, and a longer acquaintance would give another account.
Little street violence happens here, and what holds it down is an organised interest and not the watch.
The walls stand round the town, and what comes in comes in where the town chooses.
The watch walks the town at night, and the town's sense of its own safety rests on that more than on anything at the gate.
The charter hall takes the sort of trouble the watch is the wrong instrument for, and it is seldom without work.
The town keeps an arcane hand in its defences, for detection, for wards, and for what nobody at the gate can see coming.
The town walls are sound and the purse that keeps them up comes short.
